en: Ceridwen, Goddess of the Stars, of Magic,and of the Social Relationships that bind mortals together, is served by numerous cults with only tenuous ties to one another. [PARAGRAPH:2]Ceridwen first appeared to a suicidal Kylorin, asking him to worship her in exchange for arcane knowledge and the power to resurrect his wife indefinitely so they might restart their marriage untainted by her adultery. He attempted to make her cult into the State Religion of Patria, but only a small group of elites ever accepted her tenets. The most elite of the elites were the Coven of the Black Candle, whom she tasked with blotting out The Sun. This Coven consisted of Kylorin himself, Os-Gabella, Asmoday, Faeryl Viconia, Alexis, Barbatos, and "Wode"-who was actually the God of Shadow masquerading as the mortal master of Shadow magic. Esus transformed his Seven Aspects (the greatest of his True Angels besides Iaegus) into the Masks each Coven member wore, so that no power in creation could detect or control them. The members could never learn each other's identity, as the animus between Asmoday and the Fey would have made their cooperation impossible. [PARAGRAPH:1]A lesser Masked Coven, called "The Between," continues to this day. It is a small religion whose members are mostly sorceresses whose spirits, minds and occasionally bodies explore worlds beyond Erebus. Many are driven mad by the experience. They refer to their goddesses as the Maiden of the Mask. [PARAGRAPH:1]Among the Sheaim there is a cult filled with a missionary zeal to reach all nations and bring their best and brightest back to learn sorcery without the strictures and limitations placed on adepts by mage guilds in all other lands. They promise unfettered access to secret knowledge of all sorts, but tend to steer their students into the darkest of arts. The Emrys have a goal more grand that blotting our the son. They want to bring on Armageddon and end Erebus entirely. [PARAGRAPH:1]Not all of her worshipers are that evil. The Chainbreakers have more noble goals. They believe the goddess is best served by breaking unjust social bonds. They hate any relationship that is not entirely consensual. Some try to destroy marriages and turn children against their parents, but most focus their radical activism on fighting for the abolition of slavery. They can always be counted upon to provide aid and sanctuary to runaway slaves, but prefer to give them arms and help them slay their former masters. [TAB]Deep in the woods, the whispers of Elves linger. Ancient protectors normally above the affairs of men, some men have shown enough loyalty to them to be taught their magic and even gain the assistance of the Satyrs.
